prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (≤500 words, policy-only)

Public finances and tax
- Balance the structural current budget by 2017/18; set rules for debt to fall as a share of GDP (except in recessions) and balance day-to-day spending over the cycle while allowing borrowing for productive investment.
- Raise the Personal Allowance to £12,500; consider aligning the employee National Insurance threshold with the Income Tax threshold.
- No rises in headline Income Tax, National Insurance, VAT or Corporation Tax; clamp down on avoidance/evasion with a general anti-avoidance rule, tougher penalties, and action on non-domiciled status.
- Introduce a high-value property levy; maintain 0.7% of GNI for international development.

Economy, industry, energy and infrastructure
- Double economy-wide innovation/R&D over time; protect science funding; expand Catapult centres; strengthen the British Business Bank and alternative finance.
- Review Business Rates with options for Land Value Tax; complete land registration by 2020.
- Net zero greenhouse gas target by 2050; expand the Green Investment Bank with borrowing powers; increase green tax share; create an Office for Environmental Responsibility.
- Invest in rail (network electrification, HS2, East–West Rail), local light rail, and freight-to-rail; improve London and South West links; consider airport capacity without net runway increase.
- Make energy efficiency a top infrastructure priority; stimulate at least £100bn private low‑carbon investment by 2020; set a 2030 power-sector target (50–100 gCO2/kWh) and aim for 60% renewables; end unabated coal by 2025; proceed with CCS; support community energy; permit new nuclear without subsidy; targeted approach to shale with revenues for low‑carbon funds.

Trade, tech, and creative sectors
- Stay engaged in the EU single market; pursue major trade deals with protections.
- Reinstate post‑study work visas for STEM graduates; strengthen tourism support.
- Deliver 99.9% high‑speed broadband coverage; support tech clusters, scale‑ups, STEM skills, open data, and digital-by-default public services.
- Maintain free national museums; protect public service broadcasting and support creative industries.

Work, welfare, pensions, consumers
- Roll out Universal Credit; “yellow card” approach to sanctions; time‑limited 1% cap on working‑age benefit uprating (exemptions apply); restrict some pensioner benefits for higher‑rate taxpayers.
- 20 hours’ free childcare for ages 2–4 and from 9 months for working parents (phased); complete Tax‑Free Childcare and enhanced UC childcare support.
- Expand Shared Parental Leave; strengthen minimum wage enforcement; promote Living Wage in the public sector; rights on zero‑hours misuse.
- Enshrine the State Pension “triple lock”; complete auto‑enrolment; extend pension freedoms; review a single rate of pension tax relief.
- 24‑hour energy switching; smart meters; fairer rail fares; stronger consumer data portability.

Education and skills
- Protect funding from early years to 19; qualified teachers in every class; national funding formula.
- Aim to eradicate childhood illiteracy/innumeracy by 2025; independent curriculum/standards body; core PSHE (including consent, finance, first aid).
- Strengthen school leadership and accountability; local roles in place planning; no profit‑making state schools.
- Expand apprenticeships (including higher levels), National Colleges, and FE support; review HE finance; improve access and transparency.

Health, care, and public health
- Increase NHS funding in England by at least £8bn a year by 2020; pool health and social care budgets locally by 2018; expand GP access and community pharmacy.
- Establish parity for mental and physical health with waiting-time standards; invest £500m more annually by 2016/17; improve crisis care and children’s services.
- Implement the care cost cap; raise care workforce standards; support carers (annual bonus, care leave consultation).

Housing and environment
- Target 300,000 homes/year; at least 10 Garden Cities; public land release; a Housing Investment Bank; government commissioning where markets fail.
- Strengthen plan‑led development; prioritise brownfield; longer private tenancies with predictable rent increases; regulate letting fees if needed; rent deposit loans for under‑30s.
- Green Buildings Act: long‑term target for all homes to EPC Band C by 2035; low‑income and rented homes to Band C by 2027; council tax incentives; upgraded schemes for insulation.
- Five “green laws” covering nature, zero waste (70% recycling by 2025–30 timeframe), green transport (low‑emission zones; ULEV timelines), zero‑carbon target, and green buildings.

Rights, policing, justice, drugs, borders
- Digital Bill of Rights; update surveillance laws; protect encryption; new Freedoms Act; retain human rights protections.
- Replace Police and Crime Commissioners with Police Boards; Victims’ Bill of Rights; measures against violence toward women and girls.
- Presumption against short custodial sentences; expand problem‑solving courts; modernise legal aid access.
- Shift drugs policy toward treatment (Portugal model); end imprisonment for possession; allow medicinal cannabis.
- Complete entry/exit border checks; speed asylum decisions; allow work after six months; separate students in migration stats.

Devolution, democracy, media
- Cap political donations at £10,000; votes at 16; proportional voting (STV) for local and Westminster; Lords reform; stronger lobbying rules.
- Constitutional convention; implement agreed devolutions for Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland; “Devolution on Demand” in England; protect fair funding with a floor for Wales.
- Promote employee ownership and participation; strengthen community rights; modernise media plurality rules; support hyperlocal media.

International and defence
- Prioritise conflict prevention; tighten arms export controls; respond to major crises with partners.
- Conduct a Strategic Defence and Security Review; move to a Single Security Budget; reduce nuclear posture (non‑continuous patrols, fewer submarines); invest in cyber.
- Stay engaged in EU reform and trade; hold an in/out referendum only on future material treaty changes.
- Maintain 0.7% aid; drive tax transparency; support the Sustainable Development Goals; lead on climate agreements, deforestation, and marine protection; promote global human rights and freedom of belief.
